names: UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision
summary: UCSF's Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision at 490 Illinois Street, a 347,500-sq-ft eye-care facility in three buildings (a 12-story tower with a 5-story south wing and a 3-story north wing) that SF YIMBY reported open on November 27, 2020 (SmithGroup architect). The UC Regents approved a $237.13 million total project budget for it in January 2017: "The total project cost of $237.13 million (including $12 million of capitalized interest incurred during construction)"; that is a budget, not a construction cost. It stands on OCII plan block 33, between Third St and Illinois St: the City's address point for 490 Illinois St falls inside this outline, and UCSF's own 2025 campus map labels block 33 'Valley Center for Vision'. Its footprint here is approximate (see the shape's accuracy caveat).

milestones.text: The UC Regents, at their January 26, 2017 meeting, approve a $237.13 million project budget and the design of the Mission Bay East Campus Phase 1 Building (Block 33) at UCSF Mission Bay: a 12-story tower with a 5-story south wing, which the Regents' committee was told would house the Center for Vision and Neurological Sciences, and a 3-story north wing. The Regents' documents do not use the name Valley Center for Vision. The agenda item gave a proposed schedule of completion by July 2019, with construction starting in June 2017

SF YIMBY, in an article published November 27, 2020 (a publication date, not an event date), says 'A new medical facility has been opened' at 490 Illinois Street for UCSF's Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision, while also describing the building in the future tense ('The structure will contain'); the exact opening date is not given. UCSF's June 2025 Mission Bay CAC presentation (slide 2, 'MISSION BAY - EXISTING PLAN', map updated December 2024) shows 'VALLEY CENTER FOR VISION (33)' on its existing-buildings map

costs.what: Total project budget for the Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision (Block 33), as approved by the UC Regents; it includes $12 million of capitalized interest incurred during construction, so it is not a construction cost

facts.value: 490 Illinois St: the City's address point (DataSF Addresses, address ID 743049) lies inside this record's outline, on Assessor parcel 8725001, which the Assessor itself addresses as 480 16th St.
347,500 across three separate buildings (12-story tower, 5-story south wing, 3-story north wing), plus parking for over 200 vehicles across 75,000 sq ft

open_questions: No source read gives the exact opening day: SF YIMBY reported the building open on November 27, 2020, without a date.

The Regents' January 2017 documents describe the proposed Block 33 building as 343,000 gross square feet (275,400 assignable), mainly academic and administrative workspace (200,500 assignable square feet) with 45,200 assignable square feet of vision clinic space. SF YIMBY's 347,500 square feet at opening is a different figure, and no source read explains the difference.

No opening date was found for Caffe Central at 490 Illinois St: the cafe's own page (Caffe Central, '490 Illinois Street -- Mission Bay') lists the location and its hours (Monday-Friday 7am-4pm) but gives no date.

OpenStreetMap labels one of the 409/499 Illinois St buildings across Illinois St (way 84821722; tags addr:housenumber 490, addr:street Illinois Street, building:levels 6, height 28) as 490 Illinois St. The City's address point, UCSF's 2025 campus map and SF YIMBY's description all place the 12-story Valley Center for Vision here instead, so that label is not used.

Geometry: this building's east edge sits close to, but not necessarily exactly on, Illinois St's west curb line; it has not been checked against a building footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, surveyed in 2010, predates the building).
